The fix in `gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/JsonPrimitive.java:289-295`: when either `JsonPrimitive` holds a `BigInteger`, both values are now compared exactly as `BigInteger` via `getAsBigInteger()` instead of truncating to `long` via `Number#longValue()`. This fixes `JsonPrimitive(new BigInteger("23648748948963264236478263434")).equals(new JsonPrimitive(new BigInteger("808933803388026932016705674")))` returning `true`, while preserving cross-type equality (e.g. `Long(10)` still equals `BigInteger("10")`) and `hashCode` consistency for in-range integral values.
